sourceCheck: Verified on 2026-10-08: followed https://aws.amazon.com/certification/ to the current certification page, https://aws.amazon.com/certification/certified-security-specialty/, and its linked SCS-C03 guide, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/security-specialty-03/security-specialty-03.html. The revisions page lists guide version 1.0, published March 26, 2026. Separately, the comparison appendix gives SCS-C02 delivery through December 1, 2025 and SCS-C03 delivery beginning December 2, 2025. All six domain pages and every numbered Skill were read. Domain names, weights and sixteen task headings match the supplied outline: Detection 16%; Incident Response 14%; Infrastructure Security 18%; Identity and Access Management 20%; Data Protection 18%; Security Foundations and Governance 14%. The appendix abbreviates some headings; the domain pages determine exact wording. The in-scope, out-of-scope and technologies pages were read. The non-exhaustive security-aspects exception does not override the explicit Amazon MWAA and AWS Payment Cryptography exclusions. Maintenance, sunset and full-shutdown lists were checked. Excluded stale examples include CloudTrail Lake, AWS Audit Manager, Systems Manager Incident Manager and Change Manager, Amazon SNS Message Data Protection, Amazon Q Business, S3 Glacier Direct and Glacier Vault Lock, WAF Classic, Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins, Inspector Classic and CodeGuru Security. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake-service-availability-change.html specifies CloudTrail Lake closure to new customers on May 31, 2026; March 31 is its maintenance announcement date. Trails and Insights remain supported. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/codeguru-security/ specifies discontinuation on November 20, 2025 despite the guide's example. The Q Developer IDE notice specifies support ending April 30, 2027; sunset status warrants exclusion now. Current documentation distinguishes AWS Security Hub signal correlation from AWS Security Hub CSPM posture checks. Unresolved official wording conflicts: the certification page lists multiple choice/multiple response while the guide also lists ordering/matching; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/scanning-ec2.html describes both hybrid automatic enablement and agent-based default scanning for new accounts; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/Subscriptions.html lists five log-group subscription filters while https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_PutSubscriptionFilter.html lists two. WAF Classic remains on the sunset list despite its October 7, 2026 support end. No card depends on these disputed claims.

cards.statement: Amazon GuardDuty automatically consumes CloudTrail management events independently of customer trails.
cards.explanation: GuardDuty receives its own stream of CloudTrail management events. Changing a customer trail's configuration leaves that detection stream independent.

source.title: GuardDuty foundational data sources

cards.statement: Amazon GuardDuty can send newly suppressed findings to Amazon EventBridge for downstream alerting.
cards.explanation: GuardDuty automatically archives findings matched by suppression rules and excludes those findings from EventBridge delivery.
cards.misconception: Suppression hides findings in the console while preserving their downstream alerts.

source.title: Suppression rules in GuardDuty

cards.statement: A GuardDuty administrator can delay initial finding alerts by changing the finding publishing frequency.
cards.explanation: GuardDuty sends initial findings to EventBridge in near real time. The configurable publishing frequency governs subsequent occurrences.
cards.misconception: The publishing frequency also controls the first alert for a finding.

source.title: Processing GuardDuty findings with Amazon EventBridge

cards.statement: Amazon Macie's automated discovery favors previously analyzed sensitive buckets over eligible unanalyzed buckets.
cards.explanation: Macie's automated discovery prioritizes coverage of buckets it has yet to analyze over buckets where it has already found sensitive data.
cards.misconception: Automated discovery concentrates first on buckets already known to contain sensitive data.

source.title: How automated sensitive data discovery works

cards.statement: Scheduled Amazon Macie jobs automatically analyze qualifying S3 objects added or changed since the preceding run.
cards.explanation: Subsequent runs of a scheduled Macie job analyze newly created or modified objects that match its scope, keeping periodic assessments incremental.

source.title: Scope options for sensitive data discovery jobs

cards.statement: Some Amazon Macie managed data identifiers require nearby keywords to detect sensitive data in S3 objects.
cards.explanation: Certain Macie identifiers need contextual keywords as well as a matching value. In structured data, a field or column name can provide that context.

source.title: Keyword requirements for managed data identifiers

cards.statement: AWS Security Hub combines threat, vulnerability, and posture signals when it prioritizes security risks.
cards.explanation: Security Hub correlates and enriches signals to highlight critical security issues, giving responders context beyond isolated findings.

source.title: AWS Security Hub

cards.statement: AWS Security Hub CSPM cross-Region aggregation automatically enables the service in linked Regions.
cards.explanation: Cross-Region aggregation collects data from Regions where Security Hub CSPM is enabled. The aggregation configuration does not enable the service there.
cards.misconception: Linking a Region for finding aggregation also activates Security Hub CSPM in that Region.

source.title: Understanding cross-Region aggregation in Security Hub CSPM

cards.statement: CloudWatch anomaly detection can account for recurring weekly patterns in a security metric's expected range.
cards.explanation: CloudWatch's anomaly model learns recurring metric patterns. A regular weekly change can therefore fall within its expected band.

source.title: Using CloudWatch anomaly detection

cards.statement: A CloudWatch composite alarm automatically inherits the notification actions of its underlying alarms.
cards.explanation: Engineers configure actions on the composite alarm itself. Its underlying alarms contribute their states, rather than their notification actions.
cards.misconception: Combining alarms copies their configured notification actions to the composite alarm.

source.title: Composite alarms

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs metric filters with a zero default automatically emit zero while log ingestion is idle.
cards.explanation: A metric filter's default applies when logs arrive but fail to match. If no logs arrive, the filter emits no default value, so silence is distinct from zero events.
cards.misconception: A zero default proves the event count is zero even when log ingestion stops.

source.title: Creating metrics from log events using filters

cards.statement: AWS Systems Manager lets explicit inventory associations override global ones created outside Quick Setup.
cards.explanation: When explicit and non-Quick Setup global inventory associations overlap, Systems Manager gives the explicit association priority for those nodes.

source.title: Troubleshooting Systems Manager Inventory

cards.statement: CloudTrail event history in a management account aggregates events from AWS Organizations member accounts.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail event history belongs to one account and Region; a management-account search excludes member-account events.
cards.misconception: The management account's event history includes organization-wide activity.

source.title: Working with CloudTrail event history

cards.statement: An active CloudTrail trail records Amazon S3 object access by default for buckets in its account.
cards.explanation: The default trail selection covers management events. Recording Amazon S3 object access requires selecting data events.
cards.misconception: A default trail includes Amazon S3 object-level activity.

source.title: Understanding CloudTrail events

cards.statement: CloudTrail automatically adds an organization trail to new member accounts with the trail's home Region enabled.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail propagates an organization trail to joining accounts in covered Regions, so new accounts inherit its logging configuration.

source.title: Creating a trail for an organization

cards.statement: Member-account administrators outside CloudTrail delegated administration can stop organization trail logging.
cards.explanation: A member account outside CloudTrail delegated administration can view an organization trail but cannot stop or change its logging.
cards.misconception: Local member-account administrators control the organization's trail for their account.

source.title: Creating a trail for an organization

cards.statement: CloudTrail network activity events can capture API requests rejected by a supported VPC endpoint's policy.
cards.explanation: For supported services, CloudTrail network activity events include endpoint-policy denial details such as VpceAccessDenied.

source.title: Understanding CloudTrail events

cards.statement: Amazon Security Lake normalizes logs from native AWS sources into the OCSF schema.
cards.explanation: Security Lake maps natively supported AWS logs to OCSF, allowing consumers to correlate equivalent fields across sources.

source.title: What is Amazon Security Lake?

cards.statement: Amazon Security Lake query-access subscribers analyze source data through AWS Lake Formation tables.
cards.explanation: Query-access subscribers use Lake Formation tables with engines such as Amazon Athena. Security Lake identifies this access type as LAKEFORMATION.

source.title: Managing query access for Security Lake subscribers

cards.statement: Amazon Security Lake permits a rollup Region to contribute consolidated data to another rollup Region.
cards.explanation: Security Lake excludes rollup Regions from acting as contributors to another rollup Region, preventing chained aggregation.
cards.misconception: A hierarchy of rollup Regions forwards already consolidated security logs.

source.title: Configuring rollup Regions in Security Lake

cards.statement: VPC Flow Logs include traffic from EC2 instances to the Amazon DNS server.
cards.explanation: VPC Flow Logs omit instance traffic to the Amazon DNS server, leaving a gap in that evidence source.
cards.misconception: VPC Flow Logs capture instance queries to Amazon's DNS server.

source.title: Flow log limitations

cards.statement: Amazon Route 53 Resolver query logs can include repeated queries that Resolver answers from its cache.
cards.explanation: Resolver query logging omits queries answered from the Resolver cache, so repeated requests during a cached answer's lifetime may leave no new log entry.
cards.misconception: Resolver query logs provide a record of repeated queries served from cache.

source.title: Resolver query logging

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs subscription filters can match transformed events when an active log transformer is configured.
cards.explanation: With an active transformer, applyOnTransformedLogs=true makes a subscription filter evaluate transformed events, keeping downstream selection aligned with normalized fields.

source.title: PutSubscriptionFilter

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs Insights lets a monitoring account query linked source accounts' logs in the same Region.
cards.explanation: CloudWatch cross-account observability lets a monitoring account run one Logs Insights query across log groups in linked source accounts.

source.title: Analyzing log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights

cards.statement: A Lambda function's resource-based policy can grant its runtime permission to publish CloudWatch Logs events.
cards.explanation: Lambda uses its execution role's CloudWatch Logs permissions for runtime log delivery, including logs:PutLogEvents.
cards.misconception: A function's resource-based policy supplies its runtime's CloudWatch Logs permissions.

source.title: Sending Lambda function logs to CloudWatch Logs

cards.statement: Disabling AWS STS in a Region can block API Gateway's CloudWatch Logs role assumption for REST APIs.
cards.explanation: API Gateway assumes its CloudWatch Logs role through AWS STS. Regional STS settings therefore affect this REST API logging path.

source.title: Set up CloudWatch logging for REST APIs in API Gateway

cards.statement: AWS log delivery uses delivery.logs.amazonaws.com for CloudFront standard logging (v2) writes to Amazon S3.
cards.explanation: The S3 destination bucket policy for CloudFront standard logging (v2) authorizes delivery.logs.amazonaws.com to write log objects.

source.title: Configure standard logging (v2)

cards.statement: VPC Flow Logs requires a customer managed key ARN for an Amazon S3 destination that uses SSE-KMS.
cards.explanation: An SSE-KMS flow-log destination uses a customer managed key ARN. Configuring a bare key ID can produce a LogDestination undeliverable error.

source.title: Required key policy for use with SSE-KMS

cards.statement: An organization trail's presence in a member account proves CloudTrail can deliver that account's logs.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail creates member-account trail copies even when destination permissions fail validation; trail presence alone does not establish successful delivery.
cards.misconception: A visible organization trail proves its delivery permissions are valid.

source.title: Creating a trail for an organization

cards.statement: CloudTrail's organization trail role needs permission to write organization-prefixed CloudWatch Logs streams.
cards.explanation: Organization-trail log streams use the organization ID prefix. A role policy scoped to account-prefixed streams misses those streams.

source.title: Role policy document for CloudTrail to use CloudWatch Logs for monitoring

cards.statement: The CloudWatch agent can use different IAM roles to deliver logs and metrics to separate target accounts.
cards.explanation: The agent supports separate role_arn values for logs and metrics. Successful metric delivery therefore does not establish permission for the logs role.

source.title: Common scenarios with the CloudWatch agent

cards.statement: The CloudWatch agent sends EC2 metrics to the instance's Region when its configuration selects another Region.
cards.explanation: For an EC2 host, the CloudWatch agent's configured region selects the metric destination. The instance's Region supplies the default when that setting is absent.
cards.misconception: The EC2 instance's Region overrides the CloudWatch agent's configured metric destination.

source.title: Manually create or edit the CloudWatch agent configuration file

cards.statement: CreateResolverQueryLogConfig automatically selects the Region's existing VPCs for DNS query logging.
cards.explanation: CreateResolverQueryLogConfig sets the destination. AssociateResolverQueryLogConfig selects a VPC for query-log collection.
cards.misconception: Creating a Resolver logging configuration automatically selects VPCs for collection.

source.title: CreateResolverQueryLogConfig

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs can replay subscription events rejected with AccessDeniedException after permissions are repaired.
cards.explanation: AccessDeniedException is non-retryable. CloudWatch Logs temporarily disables the subscription filter and skips incoming logs during that period.
cards.misconception: CloudWatch Logs preserves rejected subscription events for replay after permission repairs.

source.title: Real-time processing of log data with subscriptions

cards.statement: CloudWatch can use cloudwatch.amazonaws.com for KMS access when publishing alarms to encrypted Amazon SNS topics.
cards.explanation: Alarm publication requires the SNS topic's customer managed key policy to grant cloudwatch.amazonaws.com kms:GenerateDataKey* and kms:Decrypt.

source.title: Managing Amazon SNS encryption keys and costs

cards.statement: Enabling CloudTrail log file validation creates digests for logs delivered while validation was disabled.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail produces no digest files for logs delivered during a disabled validation interval, even if an administrator later enables validation.
cards.misconception: Enabling validation backfills integrity digests for earlier log delivery.

source.title: UpdateTrail

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation lets IAM roles act as designated approvers for an aws:approve runbook step.
cards.explanation: An aws:approve step accepts IAM role ARNs as approvers. A response plan can therefore assign approval authority through prepared roles.

source.title: aws:approve – Pause an automation for manual approval

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation manual mode lets an engineer start the remaining steps together after the first step.
cards.explanation: Manual execution pauses between runbook steps. Responders explicitly start the next step after reviewing the previous step's result.
cards.misconception: Manual mode gates the first step and then runs the rest of the runbook automatically.

source.title: Run an automation step by step

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation can undo completed containment changes by default when an execution is canceled.
cards.explanation: Canceling an automation does not provide automatic rollback. Engineers define an onCancel workflow for the cleanup or recovery actions their response plan needs.
cards.misconception: Canceling a response runbook automatically undoes its completed changes.

source.title: Systems Manager Automation actions reference

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation lets in-flight targets finish after an execution reaches its error threshold.
cards.explanation: An Automation error threshold stops dispatch to additional targets. In-flight executions can complete and contribute further failures.

source.title: Control automations at scale

cards.statement: Step Functions Asynchronous Express Workflows provide exactly-once execution for containment runbooks.
cards.explanation: Asynchronous Express Workflows use at-least-once execution. Containment actions need to tolerate an execution running again.
cards.misconception: Asynchronous Express Workflows guarantee a containment workflow runs once.

source.title: Choosing workflow type in Step Functions

cards.statement: Step Functions Express Workflows support .sync tasks that wait for a forensic collection job to finish.
cards.explanation: Express Workflows exclude the .sync integration pattern. A response workflow that waits for a supported job through .sync uses a Standard Workflow.
cards.misconception: Express Workflows support job-completion integration through .sync.

source.title: Choosing workflow type in Step Functions

cards.statement: Step Functions requires task-token callbacks from principals in the workflow's AWS account.
cards.explanation: A task token accepts a callback from a principal in the workflow's account. Cross-account responders assume an authorized role there before returning the token.

source.title: Discover service integration patterns in Step Functions

cards.statement: Step Functions applies a containment Task's matching Retry policy before its matching Catch handler.
cards.explanation: A Task with both handlers retries the matching failure first. Its Catch transition runs after the retry policy fails to resolve that error.

source.title: Handling errors in Step Functions workflows

cards.statement: AWS Fault Injection Service uses CloudWatch alarms as configured stop conditions in response-testing experiments.
cards.explanation: An AWS FIS stop condition halts an experiment when its configured CloudWatch alarm triggers, placing a measurable guardrail on a response test.

source.title: Stop conditions for AWS FIS

cards.statement: AWS FIS selects tagged experiment targets when an engineer creates the experiment template.
cards.explanation: AWS FIS resolves targets when the experiment starts. Tag changes between template creation and execution can therefore change the resources selected.
cards.misconception: Creating an experiment template freezes its tag-selected target resources.

source.title: Targets for AWS FIS

cards.statement: Engineers can deploy Automated Forensics Orchestrator for Amazon EC2 and EKS in a central forensic account.
cards.explanation: The guidance deploys orchestration components in a forensic account and establishes trust with application accounts for prepared cross-account collection.
tags: Automated Forensics Orchestrator for Amazon EC2 and EKS

source.title: Deployment overview

cards.statement: Systems Manager Automation location concurrency caps the resources processed within a target account.
cards.explanation: Location concurrency controls concurrent account-Region pairs. Resource concurrency within a pair is a separate rate control for limiting remediation impact.
cards.misconception: The location concurrency setting limits simultaneous resource changes inside an account.

source.title: Running automations in multiple AWS Regions and accounts
